text.p: BZW, the investment banking arm of Britain's Barclays Plc, sees European economic and monetary union (EMU) as a huge opportunity but does not plan to be all things to all people, the head of its global markets division said on Thursday.

"Certainly the way we are looking at our expansion, becoming more of an international force, we're not trying to become all things to all men," Bob Diamond told reporters after addressing an industry conference on global investment banking.

While he did not detail which areas BZW would be targeting, Diamond said there were markets where clients were already well served and margins low which it might not be appropriate for BZW to attempt to service.
Diamond admitted BZW faced competition from a number of European firms but said that the opportunities were "fantastic".
He said the main significance of EMU was the disintermediation of the banks -- linking networks --, the breaking down of borders, and the development of a non-governmental corporate market.
Within this context Diamond said BZW would be able to leverage skills it already had in the sterling bond market, using its people, technology and European client base.
This involved integrating various asset classes including bonds and loans.
"Integration is key. Are you going to be an integrated investment bank or an agglomeration of boutiques? In my view an agglomeration of boutiques is not the right strategy."
Diamond reiterated the two main pillars of BZW's strategy previously outlined by chief executive Bill Harrison and the head of its parent Barclays Martin Taylor - integration and client focus.
"If you can't seamlessly integrate all your products you can't compete," he said.
Diamond admitted that recent prolonged speculation on BZW's future relationship with its parent was a nuisance but said there was no substance in the talk.
"It is not distraction in the sense that I know there is no substance to it... Having things like that talked about is a bit of a nuisance, certainly not a positive."
"But I think people know exactly what the strategy of the firm is and there is no doubt internally."
There has also been speculation on whether BZW will be able to improve profitability in the near term.
While unwilling to quantify how the investment bank had performed, Diamond said it was important to look at the year as a whole rather than the first six months to see whether progress had been made.

"Good or bad, to put too much stock on the first six months would be wrong. Whether they are pleasantly surprising or not, you need to look at how you come out of the year to see whether significant progress has been made."

He also underlined what he saw as the most important developments over the last year, centring on dramatic changes that had been implemented at BZW, starting at the very top with the appointment of Bill Harrison.
These changes needed to be given time, he said, but it was reasonable to expect progress to be made.
Diamond was also confident that BZW in its new guise would be able to cope with future cyclical downturns.
"You're going to get tough market conditions in this business once in a while... One of the goals I have is not only that we are highly profitable but that we are sustainably profitable."
He said this element was especially important within the markets division where high volatility and risk dominated.
In particular, he said the division aimed at sustaining profits whether interest rates were rising or falling by building a more sophisticated trading operation.
